lines: Ashgate used to be the last stop before the north road.
Now it is just the last stop.
Ask the gate fellow how the survey is going. Watch his face.
Under the road, is it. Under the road.
My grandmother said the same thing about the well in Marrow Hollow.

ag_kid: I am not allowed past the gate.
I have been past the gate four times.
There is nothing there. Just stakes and string and a man writing numbers.
ag_house_a: Waystation's free, you know. Always has been.
The Concord offered to pay for a new roof on it last spring.
We said no. Then we said yes. It is a very good roof.
ag_house_b: You are the one Vess sent out, then.
He wrote ahead. Three pages. Two of them were about currents.
Take care on Route 1 after dark. Things come down off the ridge.
ag_traveller: Walked in from the coast. Six days.
The sea is wrong. Flat wrong, not storm wrong.
You get out there far enough and it does not move at all.
ag_surveyor: Depth soundings. Every forty metres, all the way to the coast.
No, I do not know what we are listening for.
I know that it answers, though. Sometimes it answers.
ag_fisher: Pond is fine. Pond is normal. Pond does what a pond does.
It is the SEA that has gone strange.
Come back when you can wade. There is something on the far bank.
ag_porter: Four crates of survey stakes a week, up the north road.
Four crates a week for five weeks and the road is still closed.
You do the arithmetic. I just carry them.
